neighbours.label: commending an aim, effort or choice (laudable / commendable / noble / admirable X; 'good for you', 'more power to you'), peaking just after the praise; criticism and neutral description stay quiet
fire: Wanting to feed every child in the city is a laudable aim.
If you can afford a second home, good for you.
Anyone who gets up at five to run, more power to you.
Cutting waste in half is a commendable goal on paper.
It was a noble effort to save the old theatre.
Her wish to help the refugees is an admirable instinct.
Giving every worker a pension is a worthy idea in principle.
The mayor called the cleanup drive a praiseworthy initiative.
quiet: Wanting to tax every child in the city is a ridiculous aim.
If you can afford a second home, the agent will call you.
Anyone who gets up at five to run needs warm gloves.
Cutting waste in half is the stated goal on paper.
It was a clumsy effort to demolish the old theatre.
Her wish to help the refugees was noted in the minutes.
Giving every worker a pension is a costly idea in practice.
The mayor called the cleanup drive a pointless initiative.

notes: The card's top examples are praise conceded before a 'but'; in probes the following 'but' did not matter, the commendation did.
